newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee at 20-mth peak, July still up 15 pct.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee at 20-mth peak, July still up 15 pct.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures rallied sharply to a 20-month peak on Thursday, lifting benchmark July by almost 20 percent at one stage, on frenzied buying spearheaded by roasters, traders said.

The rally, which saw prices rising by almost 14 percent in the morning alone, gathered steam in the afternoon as New York's July arabica coffee futures whizzed past the $3 a lb mark, not seen for 20 years, minutes after the opening.
July then hit a session high of $3.18.
"The situation is getting completely out of hand but there's nothing to stop the rally," said one trader. "With the frost season starting in Brazil from this weekend, nobody wants to be short."

London's July was driven to the day's peak of $2,670 per tonne, a level not seen since September 1995, before finishing at $2,600, still a whopping $342 gain on the day. Traders said this was the single largest gain in a day in recent years.
The slight retracement followed profit taking and possibly forced liquidation following intra-day margin calls on Thursday.

This morning's buying, which followed a new advance in New York on Wednesday, gathered pace after a major roaster placed buying orders for 2,000 lots, mainly in July and September. Nestle declined to comment on traders' views that it was buying.
Other roasters also stepped-up their price-fixing as the market made its way up.
There was also market talk that a trade house was buying to cover its short positions in September and November as it could not cover its margin calls anymore.
Traders said other trade houses both small and medium were likely to follow suit if prices continue to go higher which could make the already volatile market even more violent.
The funds and speculators were also the main driving force behind this year's rally which started in January, six months before the frost season in Brazil
Traders were talking of arabicas hitting $4 or even $7 if a frost were to hit Brazil this year, with the prospect just as dramatic a drop if it does not.
"Wait until the market turns and there will be blood on the street," one said.
The London Clearing House said it has increased intra-day margin calls to two deposits of $625 each from now for all short members.
Futures volume was a sizeable 18,291 lots, centred on July and September.
Options also saw brisk activity, with 1,763 lots changing hands.
